title: Bottom temperature added a positive thermal-composition slope in three of four Northeast Shelf plankton tests
abstract: We tested whether bottom water adds a thermal-composition association beyond surface water on the Northeast US Shelf. We used NOAA EcoMon tows, fixed external thermal scores and separate tests in 1982-2001 and 2002-2023. Models controlled surface temperature, both salinities, local season, time trend, depth and sample date. Added bottom slopes were 0.079 and 0.137 index C per C in zooplankton and 0.064 and 0.137 in fish larvae. Four-test intervals were above zero in both zooplankton periods and later larvae, but not early larvae. Bottom control reduced surface slopes by 21-26% in zooplankton and 8-9% in larvae. The three positive results held with coarser cells, five-year clusters, year effects, presence weights and two-way space/time covariance. Removal of two common copepods made the early zooplankton interval cross zero. The result adds a vertical habitat test for externally scored thermal composition. It does not identify local thermal effects apart from transport or estimate a share of the terrestrial tracking gap. One shelf, selected records, coarse taxa, fixed scores and few time clusters limit inference. Code, aggregate evidence, input hashes, source terms and retrieval instructions support reproduction.
